recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Future edits should be made under specific current workflow issues for concrete resource or mapping defects rather than reopening this duplicate DSTU2 ballot comment.
issue_request: FHIR-11489 is a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 Patient Care ballot comment asking that all Patient Care resources listed on the 2016-09 workflow list follow the Workflow patterns and declare that they do so, instead of merely saying they planned to. The Jira resolution says it is a duplicate of GF#10293.
initial_application: FHIR-11489 itself had no separate source commit. The duplicate target FHIR-10293/GF#10293 contains the substantive Patient Care workflow decision, comments that documentation and gap reviews were performed, and a sequence of January-February 2017 source commits explicitly applying #10293 workflow alignment across affected Patient Care resources.
additional_context: Later workflow trackers refined the DSTU2 request: FHIR-14063 and FHIR-14064 synchronized event/request patterns, FHIR-14446 cleared later Patient Care workflow-report warnings, FHIR-19511 adjusted encounter/reported handling and exemptions, and FHIR-40500 removed ambiguous PC instantiates[x] elements in favor of workflow extensions. These later decisions explain current differences from the old wording and several are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current active build sources list the applicable Patient Care workflow resources and expose Request/Event mappings or approved mapping exceptions. Source searches found no active Patient Care resource page still saying the resources merely plan to follow workflow; the remaining generic module-level roadmap wording is not a Patient Care-specific defect.
